style.prompt:
Create a silent 15-second live-action short film in exactly three sequential scenes with clean straight cuts, about a small kindness on a damp afternoon. Photorealistic live-action cinematography, restrained naturalistic acting, gentle observational tone, sweet but never cheesy. Soft overcast daylight, muted green park, wet wood and subtle rain droplets, believable anatomy and hands. Maintain exactly the same two adult characters, outfits, park bench and geography across all scenes: a young adult woman around 25 with a curly black bob wearing a mustard-yellow raincoat, and an older man around 70 with a white beard wearing a blue coat. Neither speaks. No audio, no dialogue, no music, no titles or text.
SCENE 1, 0–5 seconds: Medium-wide eye-level shot of a wet wooden park bench beside a tree-lined path after rain. The woman approaches and stops at the bench, notices its wet seat, lightly touches the water with her fingers, then pauses with a small rueful expression. The older man stands nearby at the right end of the bench holding a neatly folded newspaper. Gentle, nearly static camera.
SCENE 2, 5–10 seconds: Cut to a closer two-shot preserving positions. The older man notices her hesitation and quietly offers his folded newspaper with a modest friendly gesture. She meets his eyes with a small grateful smile and accepts it. She lays the folded newspaper flat on the wet seat at the left half of the bench. Keep the exchange simple, unhurried and physically clear. The newspaper has indistinct printed columns, no readable headlines.
SCENE 3, 10–15 seconds: Cut to a stable medium-wide frontal two-shot. The newspaper remains beneath the woman as she sits on the left half; the man sits beside her on the right. They settle, exchange a brief warm glance and restrained genuine smiles, then look out at the park together. A quiet ordinary moment of companionship. End holding both together in frame. No exaggerated grins, no romantic implication, no sentimental visual effects, no slow motion, no montage beyond these three scenes.
